capabilities.target: HR policy search index (published policies only)

inputs.source: Employee question via SSO authenticated chat session
Published HR policy documents in the search index, authored by the HR content team under two-person publish review

instructions.note: 'Do not give legal advice' has no technical enforcement; it is a purely behavioral, model-dependent control over scope creep. See finding f2.

controls.name: Read-only credential scoped to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: The credential cannot read anything beyond the published policy index regardless of model behavior, which bounds data sensitivity reachable by the agent to internal at most.

controls.name: Network egress denied at the network layer, verified by pen test
controls.decay_rationale: No model behavior can open a network path that does not exist at the network layer; verified by pen test rather than only declared.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Removes the automated/one-click exfiltration channel for a malicious link embedded in policy text; does not remove the risk of a human manually clicking a link shown in a reply.

controls.name: Two-person review required to publish policy content
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by human process outside the model; a more capable model does not help bypass a two-person review. Can still fail under insider collusion or if new content sources skip the process.

controls.name: Model version pinned; upgrade requires a change ticket
controls.decay_rationale: Gates when a model_upgrade can occur by requiring review, but does not prevent an eventual approved upgrade from defeating dependent controls elsewhere.

controls.name: Chat replies are delivered only to the authenticated requester's own session
controls.decay_rationale: The destination is fixed by the chat platform's session identity, not chosen by the model, so it cannot be redirected to a third party regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Prompt restricts scope to published Acme HR policies and defines a fallback to the HR portal link
controls.decay_rationale: A more capable or longer-context model may reinterpret an ambiguous request as in scope, or blend retrieved text with its own reasoning beyond what was retrieved. Fails under model_upgrade, longer_task_horizon, autonomy_increase, intended_purpose_change.

controls.name: Prompt instructs the agent not to give legal advice
controls.decay_rationale: Pure instruction with no runtime enforcement. A more capable model may produce legal-sounding conclusions while believing it is only explaining policy. Fails under model_upgrade, longer_task_horizon, autonomy_increase, intended_purpose_change.

controls.name: Automated content integrity scanning of published policies before indexing
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. Would detect injected instructions or suspicious URLs independent of two-person review's reliability.

controls.name: Structural retrieval-confidence gate before free-form replies
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. Would enforce scope and the HR-portal fallback outside the model, independent of model behavior, instead of relying solely on prompt instructions.

findings.title: Compromised or malicious policy content quoted verbatim to employees (RAG/content poisoning)

attack_path.note: Internal-trust content authored by HR, published after two-person review
Agent reads the matching policy entry
Agent quotes the policy text verbatim, including any embedded link or instruction, to the employee

threat_refs.name: Context Memory Poisoning via Vector Store Contamination

forecast.watch_signal: A new ingestion source added to the policy index that bypasses two-person review, or a chat client/tool change that enables automatic link or image rendering. Either alone still leaves one of the two independent step-3 controls intact; both occurring together would remove all step-3 credit and push this toward high.

evidence.observation: Policy index holds only published policies; only the HR content team can write, and publishing requires two-person review, which is the sole upstream control against malicious or mistaken content entering the index.
Chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links, limiting but not eliminating the risk that a compromised policy entry's embedded link triggers a human-targeted phishing click.

The agent is instructed to quote the policy verbatim, so any text embedded in a policy document, including a malicious link or instruction, is reproduced directly to the employee with no technical verification step.

recommendations.action: Add automated content integrity scanning (link reputation checks, injected-instruction detection) to the HR publishing pipeline before indexing, independent of the two-person review.
Log and periodically review chat replies containing hyperlinks sourced from policy content to catch anomalous or newly introduced URLs.

Document explicit max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes in runtime config reflecting the intended single-turn design, so the inherent calculation is not driven by an undocumented-bounds default.

findings.title: Instruction-only scope enforcement allows ambiguous employee questions to drift outside intended HR-policy scope

attack_path.note: Trusted, authenticated employee asks an ambiguous or HR-adjacent legal question
Search may return a weakly relevant or no matching policy
Agent replies based only on prompt instructions not to give legal advice and to fall back to the HR portal, with no structural gate

forecast.watch_signal: Model id/version string changes in config even under the change-ticket process, or sessions trend toward longer multi-turn exchanges where scope drift accumulates, or autonomy is raised beyond A3.

evidence.observation: 'Do not give legal advice' has no runtime enforcement; it is the only control against legal-advice scope creep.
Scope ('published Acme HR policies') and the no-match fallback are defined only in the prompt, with no retrieval-confidence gate or similar structural check.
Autonomy is declared A3 with no max_unattended_steps or max_runtime_minutes stated, so these are treated as unbounded per rubric default for the inherent calculation.

recommendations.action: Add a structural retrieval-confidence gate: below a relevance threshold, automatically return the HR-portal fallback without a free-form generated answer, instead of relying on the prompt alone.
Periodically test the agent with legal-adjacent and ambiguous HR questions across model versions and tune the prompt or add response templates as needed.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is high, driven by finding f1 (internal-trust policy content quoted verbatim into a send-external sink, plus the autonomy modifier triggered by undocumented step/runtime bounds). Residual drops to moderate because two independent structural controls (two-person publish review, no image/link auto-fetch in the chat client) each credit the capped step-3 narrowing credit, and neither decays with model capability; f2 separately resolves to a residual of low because its only controls are behavioral prompt instructions, capped at the step-4 credit. The forecast ceiling stays moderate: f1 is robust because no single listed trigger defeats both of its independent structural controls at once, while f2's forecast rises back to moderate under model_upgrade, longer_task_horizon, autonomy_increase, or intended_purpose_change because its only controls (ctrl.prompt_scope, ctrl.no_legal_advice) are behavioral and dependent. The scoped read-only credential and the verified network egress denial together mean no path in this design reaches confidential/restricted data or an attacker-controlled external destination, which is why no S3/critical finding was filed.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are not documented in the runtime notes; per rubric default these were treated as null/unbounded, which elevates the computed inherent tier for S2-sink findings. If the team confirms the agent is strictly bounded to one search call plus one reply per turn, the inherent tier for those findings should be reassessed.

The two-person policy publish review and the chat client's no-image/no-autofetch behavior are recorded as declared, not independently verified (no audit log or client configuration export was provided); confidence on findings relying on them is medium.

No MCP configuration or agent card was provided; the design was treated as a single first-party agent with one local tool and no peer agents, so protocol-level checks (auth method, definition pinning) were not applicable rather than passed.
